title: Changing Almost in a Blink
summary:
Changing Almost in a Blink
As the Obama Administration continues to rev its policy engines, sacred cows of many self-interest groups may become road-kill on the United States' bio-fueled road towards energy independence. For instance, by the Administration's willingness to reconsider whether states should set auto emission limits stricter than the Environmental Protection Agency's, the bedraggled US automotive industry is now being haunted by the de facto spectre of producing cars with greater fuel efficiency. In the fuel camp, word from the EPA on how to incorporate a lifecycle analysis of the carbon footprint of fuels used to meet the Renewable Fuel Standard, is awaited anxiously.

children.title: Shoehorning in Ethanol
children.summary: To keep reformulated and conventional gasoline's ethanol content at no more than its present level of 10 percent in 2020, either an increase in the number of vehicles using E85 fuel (85 percent ethanol in hydrocarbon gasoline) or an increase in gasoline consumption is necessary. With better auto gas mileage a centerpiece of the new Administration's push towards energy independence, gasoline consumption might not see too much of a lift.

children.title: In the Year 2020
children.summary: What lies ahead for the tanker industry servicing the US in 2020? Given indications made on last year's campaign trail, one can envisage a landscape where US gasoline is forced to ingest quantities of ethanol even greater than those presently mandated.
